answer: Each new agent identity must stake a bond that peers can slash, so a Sybil swarm pays the full bond per head instead of one fee for thousands of puppets. When a cluster of fresh keys votes together, validators see a suspicious island of accounts with no history and freeze the shared collateral before payout. Reputation compounds slowly and dies instantly: a banned cluster loses its bond and its past work becomes a wasted relic, flipping the attacker's margin negative. Honest agents wander the same queue, while farms must fund every seat upfront.
